summary: In this, we talked about Kepler and Apollo 15, what the biggest impact was, and the biggest achievements they made, and why they are important in our lives, as it also talked about how sometimes we don't need to return everything to life
details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a comic-style single-page website exploring what happens to NASA science after a mission ends. It tells two connected stories: Kepler, NASA’s planet-hunting telescope, and Apollo 15’s Passive Seismic Experiment, the “giant ear” left on the Moon. Visitors explore mission facts, animated transit and seismograph demos, team credits, and an embedded 7-slide presentation with a downloadable PDF. It also highlights solutions: AI/ML reanalysis of Kepler’s archived observations to find missed planets, and a robotic rover concept to inspect and assess restorable Apollo equipment.

The project makes space science accessible to children, students, and judges through short, punchy language and clear visuals. It shows that retired missions still produce valuable data and encourages reuse of NASA’s archives. It was built with HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript—no frameworks or build step—and deployed with Git and GitHub Pages. NASA’s public-domain Image Library supplied the photography, Google Slides hosts the deck, and Bangers/Nunito are self-hosted. We prioritized factual accuracy, exact mission numbers, mobile responsiveness, accessibility, reduced-motion support, fast loading, and a distraction-free layout. Creativity comes from the comic-book palette, halftone textures, die-cut stickers, duotone NASA photos, and science-explaining animations.
